name: Ulnar nerve
summary: The terminal branch of the medial cord (C8–T1) descends on the medial side of the arm, passes behind the medial epicondyle in the cubital tunnel (where it is palpable and vulnerable), enters the forearm between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, supplies that muscle and the ulnar half of flexor digitorum profundus, and crosses the wrist superficial to the flexor retinaculum through Guyon's canal to supply most of the small muscles of the hand (interossei, medial lumbricals, hypothenar muscles, adductor pollicis) and sensation to the little finger and half the ring finger. Its dorsal cutaneous branch arises above the wrist, so dorsal ulnar hand sensation separates elbow from wrist lesions.

anatomy.location: Medial arm on coracobrachialis, then behind the medial intermuscular septum, through the cubital tunnel behind the medial epicondyle, down the medial forearm under flexor carpi ulnaris with the ulnar artery, through Guyon's canal at the wrist lateral to the pisiform, into the hand as superficial (sensory) and deep (motor) branches.

subdivisions.name: Forearm branches
subdivisions.note: flexor carpi ulnaris, flexor digitorum profundus to ring and little fingers

subdivisions.name: Dorsal cutaneous branch
subdivisions.note: dorsal ulnar hand; arises 5–8 cm above the wrist

subdivisions.name: Superficial terminal branch
subdivisions.note: palmaris brevis, sensation of little finger and medial half of ring finger

subdivisions.name: Deep terminal branch
subdivisions.note: hypothenar muscles, interossei, medial two lumbricals, adductor pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis (deep head)

function: Finger abduction and adduction, thumb adduction, flexion of the ring and little fingers, power grip and fine finger control; sensation of the medial one and a half digits and the ulnar hand.

imaging.normalAppearance: Peripheral nerves of the limbs are outside the MNI brain volume; no atlas mesh is shown. Ultrasound and MR neurography image the nerve directly; electrodiagnosis localizes the lesion functionally. Elbow ultrasound and MRI show nerve enlargement at the cubital tunnel, subluxation over the epicondyle, and denervation of the interossei and flexor digitorum profundus.

pathology.finding: Enlarged nerve at or just proximal to the medial epicondyle; nerve conduction shows focal slowing across the elbow segment.
Ganglion or hamate fracture compressing the deep branch with intrinsic denervation and spared dorsal sensation.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Nerve conduction studies across the elbow; ultrasound; MRI of the wrist for Guyon's canal

lesionEffects.deficit: Numbness of the little finger and half the ring finger, weak finger abduction, wasting of the first dorsal interosseous
lesionEffects.mechanism: Ulnar nerve at the elbow (cubital tunnel), the commonest site

lesionEffects.deficit: Claw hand (ulnar paradox: worse with distal lesions)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of lumbricals to ring and little fingers; profundus preserved in wrist lesions makes the claw worse

lesionEffects.deficit: Froment sign: thumb flexes when pinching paper
lesionEffects.mechanism: Adductor pollicis weakness compensated by flexor pollicis longus (median)
Deep branch lesion in Guyon's canal (cyclist's palsy)

examination: Finger abduction against resistance and first dorsal interosseous bulk
Froment sign and Wartenberg sign (abducted little finger)
Sensation on the little finger, and on the dorsal ulnar hand to separate elbow from wrist
Tinel at the elbow; elbow flexion test
Flexor digitorum profundus to the little finger (spared in wrist lesions)
pearls: Dorsal ulnar hand numbness means the lesion is above the wrist; normal dorsal sensation with intrinsic weakness means Guyon's canal
Hand intrinsic wasting with normal sensation everywhere should raise motor neuron disease or a C8–T1 lesion, not just an ulnar palsy

pitfalls: Lower trunk plexopathy and C8–T1 radiculopathy also waste the hand, but they involve median-innervated thenar muscles and medial forearm sensation too
